label: Artois c.1290-1300 interval on the mapped EU5 support footprint
interval_semantics: The Derville density and potential range are transformed to the exact calibrated EU5 area used by the aggregate scorer. The 4 percent residual historical-boundary area is not silently dropped or inflated; it remains explicit crosswalk uncertainty. The transformed population interval is 0.96-1.056 million and the potential capacity interval is 1.056-1.409688 million people.
pressure_evidence: Derville 1999, chapter IV, pp. 65-77: c.1300 rural density, small holdings, 75 percent cultivated land and a full/overpopulated agrarian world.
Derville 1987, Annales 42, pp. 1411-1432: tithe-yield evidence around Saint-Omer, Bethune, Lille and Douai c.1300.
Fossier and Fossier 1955, pp. 436-447: independent Artois/Flandre grain-crisis and subsistence-pressure evidence.
boundary_description: Medieval Artois agricultural core represented by the contiguous EU5 Lower Artois and Upper Artois historical provinces.
boundary_source: Derville 1999, chapter IV and chapter VIII, with the EU5 historical province crosswalk.
notes: Append-only support-area revalidation. This is a general crosswalk contract, not an Artois-specific multiplier and not a starting-population target.
